docs/Spec/Doc 05 — Mastery, KPI Rollups, Projections & Audit (Parent).md:616:**Module-1-only partials do not feed mastery.** A section requires both modules submitted (or the equivalent finalization signal per Doc 04A V2.2) to reach `submitted` state. Module-1-only completion is NOT eligible mastery evidence in V1.0. If a future V1.x wants to admit Module-1-only evidence, it must introduce a separate weaker source classification or an explicit lower-weight evidence class — out of scope for V1.0. \<\!-- RB-05P-V1-04 \--\>
docs/Spec/Doc 05 — Mastery, KPI Rollups, Projections & Audit (Parent).md:879:| V1.0 | 2026-05-13 | Claude (drafted), Karl (locked) | V1.0 LOCKED. Mastery formula: macro-average across sources of per-source weighted accuracy, with position-based recency decay (POSITION\_HALF\_LIFE \= 30 events), numerator-only difficulty weights (easy=0.79, medium=1.0, hard=1.20), MIN(1.0, …) per-source clamp, and renormalization for missing sources. 5-event threshold (MIN\_EVENTS\_FOR\_MASTERY \= 5\) for an entity (skill or domain) before mastery is computed. Skill mastery and domain mastery computed independently from the underlying event stream (not as weighted averages of each other). Source weights 0.50 / 0.30 / 0.20 (test/practice/review). 5-tier mastery levels at 0.19 / 0.39 / 0.59 / 0.79. Canonical difficulty enum is 1-3 (not 1-5). 9 hard invariants, bottom-up derivation contract, determinism guarantee, parameter versioning, 5 cross-doc seams, audit lifecycle separation from Doc 04D. Legacy EMA-shape constants (`alpha`, `delta_*`), Bayesian-prior constants (`ALPHA0`, `BETA0`), and calendar-day decay (`HALF_LIFE_DAYS`) explicitly out of V1.0 scope. Formula validated via 22-scenario numerical stress test and external cross-validation against three independent formula proposals (Kish ESS / δ\_max-in-denominator / L-DWC with K constant). **In-lock-cycle cleanup applied** (no version bump per Doc 04 family precedent): 5 reviewer blockers (RB-05P-V1-01 §8.4 calendar-decay contradiction removed; RB-05P-V1-02 half-life prose off-by-one fixed; RB-05P-V1-03 Doc 04 seam corrected to `test_session_answers` join chain, post-finalization not post-scoring, no score\_run-success gate; RB-05P-V1-04 partial-section eligibility tightened to submitted-section-only, Module-1-only excluded; RB-05P-V1-05 "not pushed from event handlers" wording clarified) \+ 3 reviewer highs (RB-05P-V1-06 canonical 1-3 difficulty enum affirmed with explicit pushback on 1-5 model; RB-05P-V1-07 macro-average truth-anchor property documented as intentional design; RB-05P-V1-08 constants versioning tightened with `constants_snapshot_hash` per-row contract) \+ 2 reviewer mediums (RB-05P-V1-09 KPI rollups clarified as materialized derivatives; RB-05P-V1-10 status flip back to Draft for cleanup, then re-locked) \+ 4 extensions for items added during 05A pre-draft Q\&A (RB-05P-V1-11 05A pre-implementation RPC verification gate added; RB-05P-V1-12 guardian exposure constraint added to §18 acceptance criteria; RB-05P-V1-13 `DIAGNOSTIC_TOTAL_QUESTIONS` recomputed as `N_canonical_domains × MIN_EVENTS_FOR_MASTERY = 8 × 5 = 40` so a completed diagnostic clears per-domain threshold for every SAT domain; RB-05P-V1-14 acceptance criterion \#20 added locking student/guardian read surfaces to `mastery_level` only — `mastery_score` and `mastery_pct` are admin/internal/audit-only). |

docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:14:* **BLK-V2-02 — Vertex schema vs 03C→03B response schema split.** V2.0 §5.5 Vertex `responseSchema` still required `related_question_canonical_id`, but §5.9 candidate-slots flow says the model returns `related_candidate_slot_id` and 03C resolves canonical IDs server-side. V2.1 splits: §5.5 Vertex output schema requires `related_candidate_slot_id` only; new §7.1.1 documents the post-Vertex 03C → 03B response schema with resolved canonical IDs.  
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:16:* **BLK-V2-04 — Remove `ORDER BY RANDOM()` from candidate pre-select.** V2.0 §5.9.2 used `ORDER BY ... RANDOM()` which violates deterministic replay/debuggability. V2.1 replaces with seeded deterministic ordering using `hashtext(canonical_id || student_id || current_date::text)`; same-day candidates are stable for a given student, allowing reproducible debugging.  
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:689:**No canonical ID exposure to the model:** per 03A V3 §11.2, canonical question IDs are internal-only. 03C does not pass `source_question_canonical_id` into the prompt body; it passes question content (stem, options, correct answer where context allows per 03B §16 anti-leak rules) without the ID string. ID stays in request metadata for 03C's own cache key computation.
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:691:**Similar-question candidate IDs are opaque slot IDs, not canonical IDs.** Per §5.9 candidate-slots flow, when the model is asked to propose a similar question, 03C passes pre-selected candidates tagged with opaque `slot_1`, `slot_2`, etc. The model returns a slot\_id; 03C resolves to canonical\_id server-side. The model never sees canonical IDs.
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:914:      "description": "V2.1 (BLK-V2-02): Vertex output uses opaque candidate slot IDs only; 03C resolves to canonical IDs post-Vertex per §7.1.1. The model never produces canonical IDs.",  
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1024:V1 response schema required `related_question_canonical_id` in `question_links[]`, but §4.4 prohibits passing canonical IDs to the model. V1.1 resolves via **candidate-slots flow** (option a; option c semantic-search deferred to V2 per hybrid decision).
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1089:**Determinism guarantee (V2.1):** for a given `(source canonical_id, student_id, current_date)` tuple, the candidate ordering is stable. Two invocations of the same student turning to the same source question on the same day will receive the same candidate slot ordering. This enables:
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1101:Candidates are assigned opaque slot IDs (not canonical IDs) and passed to the model as structured context:
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1144:**Model's responsibility:** pick the slot\_id that matches the intended similar question (or omit the question\_link entry if none is appropriate). Model MUST NOT hallucinate canonical IDs.
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1146:**03C's responsibility (post-model):** resolve each `related_candidate_slot_id` to the candidate's `canonical_id` and `question_row_id`; fill the response `question_links[]` entries accordingly. If model returns a slot\_id not in the candidate list (hallucination), 03C drops that `question_links[]` entry and logs drift via `vertex_candidate_slot_hallucination_rate` SLI.
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1150:The `source_question_canonical_id` and `source_question_row_id` fields come from envelope's `resolved_scope`, not from model output:
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1511:The model never sees or produces canonical IDs. Per §4.4 internal-only rule \+ §5.9 candidate-slots flow:
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1575:* Anti-leak: model never sees canonical IDs, satisfying §4.4  
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1577:* Validation: 03C can validate `related_candidate_slot_id` against its known candidate list before resolving; hallucinated slots are detected (not silently passed through as garbage canonical IDs)  
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1606:* Must include `source_question_canonical_id` for every link (03C enforces)
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1717:### **7.4.5 Canonical ID resolution in streaming**
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:1719:`question_link` events in the stream carry `related_candidate_slot_id` (opaque slot ID per §5.9), NOT `related_question_canonical_id`. 03B receives the stream and resolves slot\_ids to canonical\_ids post-stream (or during stream for pass-through-to-client). This maintains the §4.4 "no canonical IDs to model" rule in streaming mode.

docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:2733:* \[ \] **V2.1: 03C → 03B response schema (§7.1) populates `related_question_canonical_id` via §7.1.1 resolution flow**  
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:2736:* \[ \] **V2.1: Candidate pre-select (§5.9.2) uses deterministic `hashtext(canonical_id || student_id || current_date)` ordering — no `RANDOM()`**  
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:3870:**CR-03C-V1.1-02** `[ADDITIVE][NO-MIGRATION]` — BLK-03C-02 closeout (hybrid option d). §5.9 candidate-slots flow added for V1: 03C pre-selects 3-5 candidate similar questions server-side; passes as opaque slot IDs to model; model returns slot\_id; 03C resolves to canonical\_id. Preserves §4.4 canonical-ID-internal-only rule. V2 target (semantic-search description-matching) deferred. New SLIs: `candidate_preselect_latency_p95`, `candidate_preselect_empty_rate`, `vertex_candidate_slot_hallucination_rate`, `similar_question_offer_rate`.
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:3880:**CR-03C-V1.1-07** `[ADDITIVE][NO-MIGRATION]` — AMB-03C-04 closeout. §7.4 fully rewritten with SSE wire format specification. Content-Type, event types (content\_delta, suggested\_action\_set, ui\_hints\_set, question\_link, instruction\_exposure, orchestration\_meta, error, done), data payload shapes, event ordering guarantees, canonical ID resolution in streaming, failure mode, V1 opt-out posture, no-state-mutation rule.
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:3948:**CR-03C-V2.1-02** `[ADDITIVE][NO-MIGRATION]` — BLK-V2-02 closeout. Vertex output schema (§5.5) and 03C → 03B response schema (§7.1) explicitly split. New §7.1.1 documents the split: Schema A (Vertex output) uses opaque `related_candidate_slot_id` only; Schema B (03C → 03B response) is post-resolution with canonical IDs filled by 03C from envelope \+ candidate list lookup. §5.5 `responseSchema` for question\_links updated to drop canonical ID fields and require slot ID \+ relationship\_type \+ reason\_code only. Hallucinated slot handling specified (drop link, log SLI, turn succeeds).
docs/Spec/Doc 03C — GCP Orchestration.md:3952:**CR-03C-V2.1-04** `[REFACTOR][NO-MIGRATION]` — BLK-V2-04 closeout. §5.9.2 candidate pre-select query replaces `ORDER BY ... RANDOM()` with `ORDER BY ... hashtext(canonical_id || student_id || current_date::text)`. Provides deterministic same-day ordering per (source-question, student) for replay/debug; varies across days for natural diversity rotation. Determinism guarantee documented in V2.1 prose addition.
docs/Spec/Doc 03A — LISA Context & Memory Runtime.md:114:The SAT{M|RW}{1|2}\[A-Z0-9\]{6} canonical IDs may be stored in context payloads for retrieval and continuity, but they are never included in anything LISA outputs to students. This is INV-03-10, enforced at the output scanner (Doc 03C) and anchored here by keeping canonical IDs in internal-only context fields.

docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:26:18. Full-Length Exam Adaptive Module 2 Routing  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:57:Lyceon's runtime engines are where content becomes learning. The content supply chain governed by Doc 02A produces questions. This document governs everything that happens after — how those questions are served to students, how answers are collected, how sessions persist, how exams are scored, how tutor operates across surfaces, how reveal rules are enforced, how adaptive Module 2 routing works in full-length exams, and how runtime behavior feeds the downstream mastery and analytics layers.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:63:Build production-grade learning engines that feel fast, fair, stable, and trustworthy. The runtime should maximize student confidence (sessions behave predictably), session continuity (students never lose progress), educational value (the right questions at the right times), scoring integrity (exam results are legitimate), deterministic behavior (behavior can be explained and audited), monetization clarity (free vs paid is obvious and fair), and adaptive authenticity (full-length exams route Module 2 like the real SAT).
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:67:Runtime bugs are the most visible bugs in the product. Content errors are often caught by QA or surface slowly through complaints; runtime bugs are experienced immediately and felt acutely. A lost session, a leaked answer, a timer that misbehaves during an exam, an entitlement check that incorrectly paywalls a free feature, or an adaptive Module 2 that routes wrong — each of these is a trust-destroying event. The runtime must be the most reliable part of the system because it is the part students interact with directly and continuously.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:75:This document governs practice sessions, review sessions with spaced repetition, full-length exams with adaptive Module 2 routing, question-serving APIs, session persistence and resume, server-authoritative timers, reveal-rule enforcement, tutor runtime access rules, reaction policy (what happens after a wrong answer or a tutor request), runtime session\_items writes and their role as the canonical runtime state record, canonical event emission to the mastery engine via RPC, entitlement gating at the runtime surface, math tooling integration (Desmos, formula sheet), and the constants-in-DB contract that governs all runtime-affecting configuration values.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:105:* **PDF-04 Full-Length Exams & Scoring:** All sections on exam lifecycle, timing, scoring pipeline, domain and skill breakdown, guardian visibility for exam data, and exam API behavior. Extended here with adaptive Module 2 routing not present in the original.  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:155:* Full-length: `full_length_exam_sessions`, `full_length_exam_modules`, `full_length_exam_questions`, `full_length_exam_responses`, `full_length_exam_score_rollups` (canonical); form blueprints split between `test_forms`/`test_form_items` (legacy read) and `exam_forms`/`exam_form_items` (target write); `full_length_adaptive_config` drives Module 2 routing  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:277:| Module state | `full_length_exam_modules` | Per-module lifecycle including Module 2 routing decision |
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:283:| Adaptive config | `full_length_adaptive_config` | Module 2 routing thresholds and parameters |
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:340:* **Full-length:** Module 1 is deterministic at session creation (same for all students taking the form). Module 2 requires Module 1 outcome for adaptive routing. Prefill is two-staged: Module 1 at session creation, Module 2 at Module 1 submission after routing. §17 and §18 document this.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:362:**Full-Length Exams** are trust-anchor assessments. They simulate the real SAT with strict timing, no tutor, no mid-exam reveals, official-style scoring, and **adaptive Module 2 routing** that matches real SAT digital behavior. Full-length results inform mastery heavily because they are high-integrity signal. Students take exams periodically to measure progress, not as a daily activity.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:368:Conflating surfaces produces both bad product and bad learning outcomes. If practice and review behave identically, students don't distinguish between casual reps and deliberate concept learning. If exams feel like practice, the exam's trust-anchor value collapses. If full-length exams use static forms without adaptive Module 2, they don't match real SAT behavior and the measurement validity drops. If tutor behaves the same everywhere, students who need pre-submission reasoning help can't get it (practice reveals too early) and students who need post-submission explanation get too little help (review withholds the answer). Surface-aware design is what makes each role work.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:428:Full-length exam Module 2 routing is server-authoritative. The routing decision is computed from Module 1 raw score against thresholds in `full_length_adaptive_config` and is not influenced by client state. Clients receive the routed module's questions; clients do not choose and the routed variant label is not disclosed in API responses.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:443:4. **Prefill session items** — at session creation (for practice and full-length Module 1), the server runs selection logic once and writes all target\_count question assignments as rows in the session\_items table with a position/ordinal and denormalized snapshot. Full-length Module 2 is prefilled after Module 1 submission and routing (§18). Review does not prefill per session.  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:810:Full-length exams are Lyceon's trust anchors. They simulate the real SAT as closely as possible — fixed forms with adaptive Module 2 routing, strict timing, server-authoritative clock, no tutor, no mid-exam reveals. Students take them periodically to measure progress, not as a daily activity. Exam results inform mastery heavily because high-integrity signal is scarce and valuable.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:820:* Module 1 for Reading & Writing (static for all students)  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:821:* Module 1 for Math (static for all students)  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:822:* Module 2 for Reading & Writing — two variants: weaker and stronger  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:823:* Module 2 for Math — two variants: weaker and stronger
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:825:Each student taking the form sees both Module 1 sections and ONE of the two Module 2 variants per section, based on adaptive routing (§18).
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:829:Lyceon ships with 4 full-length forms at launch, matching Bluebook parity. Each form contains the full structured set (Module 1 \+ two Module 2 variants per section).
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:843:* Student may skip the break via an explicit "Continue to Math" action; skipping immediately ends the break and starts Math Module 1  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:844:* If the student does not skip, the break ends automatically when the break timer expires and Math Module 1 auto-starts  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:865:Exam sessions progress through states: created (session record exists, not yet started), active-module-1 (student is working Module 1 of a section), active-module-2 (routed variant active), break (between sections), completed (all modules submitted or timer expired), abandoned (created but never started within timeout).
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:869:The client requests exam session creation with a specific form identifier. The server validates authentication, validates premium entitlement (no exceptions), validates the form is published, validates no other active exam session, creates the `full_length_exam_sessions` row, creates the Module 1 rows in `full_length_exam_modules` (RW Module 1 and Math Module 1), and prefills the Module 1 questions from the form blueprint into `full_length_exam_questions` with position ordinals and denormalized snapshots.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:871:Module 2 questions are NOT prefilled at session creation. They prefill after Module 1 routing (§18).
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:890:An exam completes when all modules (RW Module 1, RW Module 2, Math Module 1, Math Module 2\) are submitted or the section timers have expired. On completion, the scoring pipeline runs immediately (§19). After scoring, review phase unlocks — the student sees correct answers, explanations, and full performance breakdown. Before completion, no reveals.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:902:# **18\. Full-Length Exam Adaptive Module 2 Routing**
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:906:Real SAT digital administration routes Module 2 based on Module 1 performance — students who performed well on Module 1 get the "harder" Module 2 variant; those who struggled get the "easier" variant. This adapts measurement precision to ability level. Lyceon implements the same pattern for SAT-authentic practice.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:910:After a student submits Module 1 of a section (RW or Math), the server:
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:912:1. Computes the raw score for Module 1 (count of correct answers)  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:914:3. Selects the routed Module 2 variant per the routing rule  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:916:5. Prefills the Module 2 questions from the form blueprint into `full_length_exam_questions`  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:917:6. Transitions the session to `active-module-2` state for that section
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:929:Routing is server-authoritative per INV-02B-14. The client does not receive and cannot influence the routing decision. The API response to the client does NOT include a `module_2_variant` field — the client receives the routed module's questions; nothing in the response discloses which variant was assigned. This prevents a sophisticated user from detecting their routing via network inspection.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:931:The `module_2_variant` field is server-only state in `full_length_exam_modules`. It is visible only to admin/operations access and in post-exam diagnostic audit.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:935:If Module 1 scoring computation fails during routing (e.g., DB error, integrity check failure):
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:945:## **Retired Questions in Module 1**
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:947:If a Module 1 question was retired between form publish and the student's exam, per INV-02B-13 the session\_item preserves the original snapshot. The question is served as normal. For routing, the student's answer against the snapshot's `correct_answer` is used — they get credit for correct answers based on what they were shown, not the current question state.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:957:* `module_2_variant_labels` — canonical labels matching form structure
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:965:* `routing_raw_score` — Module 1 raw score at routing time  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:972:## **Scoring with Module 2 Variants**
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:974:Module 2 variants have different difficulty curves. The scoring pipeline (§19) handles the variant-aware scaled score lookup. Scaled scores from the easier-variant path top out lower than scaled scores from the harder-variant path (this matches real SAT). Raw score \+ Module 2 variant determines scaled score.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:976:Students who route to the easier Module 2 cannot earn the highest scaled scores; students who route to the harder Module 2 can. This matches real SAT behavior and is not a bug — it's the adaptive measurement working as designed.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:980:The UI does not tell the student which Module 2 variant they were routed to. Real SAT doesn't either. Upon review-phase unlock, the student sees their scaled score and breakdown but not the routing label. This preserves the adaptive measurement integrity and matches how Bluebook behaves.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:984:Without adaptive Module 2, Lyceon's full-length exams don't match real SAT behavior. Students who practice on non-adaptive forms experience a different test than what they'll encounter on test day. The authenticity gap undermines the trust-anchor positioning. Adaptive Module 2 is what makes these exams SAT-grade measurement, not just "practice tests with timing."
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:988:Before refactoring adaptive routing: inspect `full_length_adaptive_config` for current thresholds and structure, verify routing logic in `fullLengthExam.ts` is server-side (not client-influenced), confirm Module 2 prefill happens after Module 1 submission (not at session creation), test that both variants exist in form blueprints and are labeled consistently, verify API response does NOT include variant label, test retired-question handling in Module 1 scoring.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1000:Per-question answer correctness from `full_length_exam_responses`, section membership, Module 2 variant per section from `full_length_exam_modules`, domain and skill metadata from session\_item snapshots.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1004:Raw section score equals count of correct answers across both Module 1 and the routed Module 2 variant for that section. Omitted questions count as incorrect per SAT scoring rules.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1060:Before refactoring scoring: inspect current `sat_score_tables` (or equivalent) for Module 2 variant awareness, verify scoring is deterministic (re-run produces same result), confirm scoring triggers mastery RPC calls, inspect UI labeling of scaled vs diagnostic signals, verify domain and skill breakdown storage matches downstream consumption expectations, test zero-raw-score edge case.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1080:* **Exam active-session question:** stem, passage, options, assets, remaining time. No correct\_answer, explanation, option\_metadata. No indication of Module 2 variant.  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1558:| Module 2 routing: raw score exactly at threshold | Per `full_length_adaptive_config.tie_break_rule` — route easier at launch |
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1559:| Module 2 routing: computation failure | Retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff; persistent failure → exam\_scoring\_pending state \+ ops alert; no default variant |
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1589:* **Exam integrity:** exam completion rate, auto-submit-on-expiry rate, reconnect rate, routing decision distribution (easier vs harder Module 2\)  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1600:* Module 2 routing: extreme distribution skew (e.g., 99% routing to easier) suggests Module 1 difficulty miscalibration  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1601:* Module 2 routing computation failures (immediate page)  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1626:* Module 2 routing tests: test both easier and harder routing paths, edge case at threshold, computation failure handling, no-variant-leakage in API responses  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1627:* Scoring pipeline tests: known answer sets produce known scaled scores deterministically, including Module 2 variant awareness and full-section omission  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1637:* ≥90% on scoring pipeline code including Module 2 routing  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1646:Run against test Supabase project, not production. Scenarios: complete practice session end-to-end, complete review attempt with SM-2 schedule update, complete full-length exam including Module 2 routing and scoring, verify reveal matrix at each endpoint, verify mastery RPC call completeness.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1682:Exam integrity enforced through: server-authoritative timer (§17), zero grace period, UI tutor absence \+ server warning (§21), module locking, review gate, Module 2 routing server-authority with no-variant-disclosure (§18).
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1694:Security-relevant actions (auth events, entitlement changes, exam tutor invocations, admin actions, Module 2 routing decisions) logged to audit trail separate from runtime logs. Retained longer, queryable for investigation.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1714:Lyceon's runtime must be tunable operationally without code deploys. Marketing wants to try 50 quota instead of 40? Config change, not deploy. SM-2 intervals need tuning based on usage data? Config change. Module 2 thresholds need adjustment based on scaled score distribution? Config change. The cost is paid once (set up tables, load code); benefit recurs every tuning decision and every operational incident.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1724:* `full_length_adaptive_config` (exists) — Module 2 routing thresholds and rules  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1748:* **Who approves:** Owner approves for their constants (product for product-owned, engineering for technical, content ops for content-owned). Founder/CTO approval required for changes affecting revenue, user experience, or integrity (quota, entitlement, exam timing, Module 2 thresholds).  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1878:High-risk changes (reveal-matrix enforcement, scoring pipeline, Module 2 routing, entitlement logic, mastery RPC contract, constants doctrine enforcement) approved at Founder \+ CTO level regardless of apparent scope.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1906:* `full_length_exam_questions` prefill timing (Module 1 at session create, Module 2 at routing)  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1915:* Module 2 variant not disclosed in API responses
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:1934:* Adaptive Module 2 routing implementation (server-side, no variant leakage)  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2093:**Previous Rule:** Exam form count unspecified. **Updated Rule:** 4 full-length forms at launch, Bluebook parity. Each form contains Module 1 \+ two Module 2 variants per section. Ramp to 6+ post-launch. **Why:** Matches official standard; achievable via 02A pipeline. **Build Impact:** Content operations produce 4 approved forms (with all Module 2 variants) before launch.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2109:**Previous Rule:** Identity canonical unclear. **Updated Rule:** `profiles` is canonical identity. `users` deprecated. Role resolution via `profiles.role` enum. **Why:** Schema audit confirms `profiles` is new canonical; `users` is Wave 1 fossil. **Build Impact:** All runtime identity reads use `profiles.id` and `profiles.role`. Wave 1 tables FK'd to `users` are legacy.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2121:**Previous Rule:** Question selection on-demand at serve time. **Updated Rule:** Session items prefilled at session creation (practice and exam Module 1). Full target\_count selected once and written to session\_items with denormalized snapshots. Serve reads from prefilled session\_items. **Why:** Deterministic, resilient to network failures, audit-friendly, testable. Tradeoff: less mid-session adaptation acceptable. **Build Impact:** Selection algorithm runs at session creation; session\_items written up-front; `/next` returns prefilled items.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2125:**Previous Rule:** Full-length exams use static forms. **Updated Rule:** Full-length uses adaptive Module 2 routing per real SAT. Forms contain Module 1 \+ two Module 2 variants per section. Routing decision based on Module 1 raw score vs `full_length_adaptive_config` threshold. Target form table: `exam_forms`; legacy: `test_forms`. **Why:** SAT-authentic behavior; matches Bluebook; adaptive measurement precision. **Build Impact:** Form blueprints contain variants; routing server-authoritative with no client disclosure; Module 2 prefilled after Module 1 submission; migration from test\_forms to exam\_forms in-flight.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2195:## **Example Two: Premium User Full-Length Exam with Adaptive Module 2**
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2199:**Exam start.** User selects test, confirms start. Server validates premium entitlement via `entitlements` read. Validates no other active exam. Reads the form blueprint from current read path (`test_forms` currently; `exam_forms` target). Form contains: Module 1 RW (28 questions), Module 1 Math (22 questions), Module 2 RW easier \+ harder variants, Module 2 Math easier \+ harder variants.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2201:Creates `full_length_exam_sessions` with started\_at=now, section durations from `exam_runtime_config`. Creates `full_length_exam_modules` rows for Module 1 RW and Module 1 Math with state='pending'. Prefills `full_length_exam_questions` with all Module 1 items (ordered per form). Module 2 NOT prefilled yet.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2203:Session state: active-module-1-rw. Timer running.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2205:**Module 1 RW.** User works through 28 questions. Server serves each question from prefilled snapshot. Client displays with remaining time. No tutor UI. No reveals.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2207:User submits final RW Module 1 answer at \~35 minutes in. Submits the module (UI "End Section"). Server locks Module 1 RW. Updates `full_length_exam_modules` row to state='completed'.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2209:**Adaptive routing for RW.** Server runs routing: counts correct answers in Module 1 RW. Reads threshold from `full_length_adaptive_config.rw_m1_threshold_raw_score`. User's raw \= 22/28; threshold \= 18\. User routes to harder Module 2 RW. Updates `full_length_exam_modules` with module\_2\_variant='harder', routing\_raw\_score=22, routing\_threshold\_used=18, routing\_config\_version='v1', routed\_at=now. Prefills `full_length_exam_questions` with the harder variant's items for RW Module 2\.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2213:**Break.** After Module 2 RW submission, user enters break. Break timer from `exam_runtime_config.break_duration_seconds` (600s). User takes 8 minutes, clicks "Continue to Math." Break ends immediately. Math Module 1 starts.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2215:**Module 1 Math.** Same flow. User answers 22 Math Module 1 questions. User has access to Desmos (collapsible panel, available on math). Formula sheet accessible. Submits Module 1 Math.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2217:**Adaptive routing for Math.** Server routes. User's Math M1 raw \= 12/22; threshold \= 14\. User routes to easier Module 2\. Prefills easier variant.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2219:**Module 2 RW.** User works through the harder variant (unknown to them which variant — API response doesn't disclose).
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2221:**Module 2 Math.** User works through the easier variant (unknown).
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2237:**Key note:** student does not see which Module 2 variants they got. Just their scaled scores. Same as real SAT. The routing audit trail lives on `full_length_exam_modules` for operations inspection if needed.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2347:| `rw_m1_threshold_raw_score` | (product decision) | 0 | 28 | Product | Raw score threshold for RW Module 2 routing |
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2348:| `math_m1_threshold_raw_score` | (product decision) | 0 | 22 | Product | Raw score threshold for Math Module 2 routing |
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02B_ Runtime Engines (V4).md:2350:| `module_2_variant_labels` | \[easier, harder\] | — | — | Product | Canonical variant labels |
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:80:The canonical scoring formula and its constants. The `scoring_constants` and `scoring_model_versions` DB tables. The `score_runs` table and its insert-once invariant. The `score_run_event_ledger` for orchestrator idempotency. The canonical PL/pgSQL function `compute_section_scaled_score` and its scoring helpers. The canonical answer-comparator function `is_answer_correct`. The difficulty-bucket schema on canonical questions (easy/medium/hard) per Doc 02. The per-module question distribution requirements enforced at form-publish time. The path floor and ceiling floor mechanics. The Module 2-only deduction model. The rounding rule. The audit trail produced on scoring including intermediate value capture and constants snapshot. The disclosure language displayed to students adjacent to scaled scores. The validation methodology used to lock v1.0 and the calibration methodology that will refine constants post-launch. The consumer-pattern integration with Doc 04A's `exam_runtime_outbox`. The partial-scoring path that handles abandoned sessions whose at-least-one section reached submitted state.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:107:- **Path is recorded, not re-derived.** Once a student is routed to Module 2A or 2B during the exam runtime, that path is persisted by Doc 04A on `test_session_sections.module2_path`. Doc 04B reads the recorded path; it does not re-derive routing.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:124:- `test_form_items(test_form_id, section, module, ordinal, question_id)` — canonical question membership per form. The set of presented questions for a session is deterministic from the form ID, section, and Module 2 path.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:126:- `test_session_sections(test_session_id, section, state, module2_path, module1_submitted_at, module1_submitted_by, module2_submitted_at, module2_submitted_by, ...)` — per-section state and the locked routing decision in `module2_path`.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:134:- `submitted` means: both modules have been submitted (by student or timeout), `module2_path` is locked, all answer state is final.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:135:- Sections in any other state (`not_started`, `module1_active`, `module1_submitted`, `module2_active`) are NOT scoreable. The scoring path MUST skip them.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:145:`module` is text, not integer. Values are `'1'` (Module 1) and `'2A'` / `'2B'` (Module 2 path-specific). All scoring queries that filter by module MUST use these text values.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:190:## **5.5 Continuous Module 1 ceiling, not discrete path math**
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:192:The formula uses Module 1 raw correct count as a *continuous* ceiling-shaper rather than a discrete path multiplier: `ceiling = max(430, 800 · (r₁/N₁)^0.5)`. This produces a smooth ceiling that rises with Module 1 performance.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:194:The path (recorded by Doc 04A on `test_session_sections.module2_path`) is read by Doc 04B for floor selection (Path B has a different floor than Path A) but is not used as a hard multiplier in the ceiling math.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:196:## **5.6 Deductions apply only to Module 2 wrong answers**
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:198:Module 1 errors lower the ceiling via the continuous power function. They do NOT additionally subtract from the score. Otherwise Module 1 errors would be counted twice.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:200:Module 2 errors apply as point deductions from the M1-determined ceiling. M1 sets the range, M2 places the student within it.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:210:Deduction weights: easy = 15, medium = 9, hard = 6. Missing a wrong easy Module 2 question costs more scaled-score range than missing a hard one. Ratio approximately 2.5:1 (Applerouth-confirmed direction for CB's IRT asymmetry). Single-miss magnitudes are smaller than Applerouth's reported magnitudes because linear scoring cannot replicate IRT's non-linear top-of-scale behavior; the direction is preserved, the absolute magnitudes are calibrated for sensible aggregation across a full Module 2.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:214:A student with very low Module 1 performance has a mathematically computed ceiling below 200 via the power function. Without a floor on the ceiling itself, such students cannot recover even with strong Module 2A.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:224:## **5.11 Path B floor scales with Module 1 margin**
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:226:Routing to Path B (Module 1 raw ≥ T) is itself evidence of baseline ability. CB-reported and community-reported Bluebook data both suggest Path B students rarely score below ~450 even when they collapse on Module 2B.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:228:V1.0 implements: `path_b_floor = min(580, 450 + 15 · (r₁ - T))`. At the threshold, the floor is 450. Each additional Module 1 correct lifts the floor by 15 points, capped at 580.

docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:424:1. The **banded ceiling** rises with Module 1 performance and cannot drop below 430. A student demonstrating ability in Module 1 unlocks higher possible scores; a student who bombs Module 1 still has a recoverable upper bound if Module 2A is strong.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:426:2. The **Module 2 deductions** erode the ceiling based on wrong-answer count weighted by difficulty. Easy wrong answers cost more than hard wrong answers (the Applerouth-confirmed asymmetry direction).
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:430:4. The **path-aware floor** rewards routing to Path B as evidence of baseline ability. It scales with Module 1 margin above threshold.
docs/Spec/Doc 04B Full length scoring V4.3/Lyceon_Doc_04B_V43.md:660:Similarly, `section_total_questions` and `module1_questions` are derivable from `test_form_items` for the session's form. They are stored in `scoring_constants` as a convenience cache only; the scoring function MAY read either source. The form is authoritative; the constants cache must match.

docs/Spec/Doc 04D — Exam Audit, Observability, Reliability & Failure Handling.md:118:1. **Every critical state transition is reconstructable from canonical state \+ audit events.** For any test session, ops MUST be able to reconstruct: who started it, which form was bound, which scoring model version was bound, when each module started / submitted / timed out, which `module2_path` was locked, which idempotency keys were replayed, which outbox events were written, whether scoring succeeded or failed, whether review was unlocked. 04D does NOT duplicate canonical data — it records audit events that, combined with canonical tables, support the reconstruction. If a transition is observable in canonical state but not via a 04D event (or vice versa), that is an audit gap.

docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:124:`test_session_sections.module2_path` is internal-only. It is captured for audit and for 04B scoring (which reads it to apply the correct M2 difficulty distribution). It MUST NOT appear in any student-facing or guardian-facing API response, report field, or UI element. Admin / audit responses MAY expose it.
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:149:3. **Routing locks at Module 1 submit.** Once a section's Module 1 is submitted (by student action or timeout), the routed Module 2 path (`A` or `B`) is written to the section row and is immutable for the lifetime of the session. Resume reads the locked path; no recomputation.  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:150:4. **Published form items are immutable.** A session bound to `test_form_id = X` always serves the same Module 1 question set, the same Module 2A set, and the same Module 2B set. Form content changes require a new form, not a mutation.  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:152:6. **Module answers lock at module submit.** Once a module's section state transitions out of `module1_active` or `module2_active` (by student submit or timeout), answer writes for that module's questions MUST be rejected with `409 module_submitted`. The schema enforces this via state-aware preconditions; no answer write can succeed against a non-active module.  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:162:16. **Partial scoring eligibility requires Module 2 submitted (V2.2 — NEW per V2.2 lock-cycle BL4).** A section is eligible for partial scoring only after its Module 2 reaches state `submitted` (whether by student-initiated submit or by Module 2 timeout). Module 1 submission alone — whether student-submitted or auto-routed by Module 1 timeout — does NOT produce a scoreable partial section. A session abandoned with one section in `module1_submitted` and the other section in `submitted` ends as `partial_scored_abandoned`, but the partial-scoring outbox payload (§14.4) flags the `module1_submitted` section as not-scored. A session abandoned with BOTH sections only in `module1_submitted` ends as `abandoned_final` (no scoreable section) — the sweep classifies on `submitted` count, not `module1_submitted` count.

docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:928:## **9\. Module 1 → Module 2 routing**
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:932:When Module 1 of a section is submitted (whether by student action via `POST /api/tests/sessions/:session_id/sections/:section/modules/1/submit` or by the timeout path in §8.4):
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:934:1. The handler computes Module 1 raw score: count of `test_session_answers` rows where `test_session_id = $session AND section = $section AND module = '1'` whose stored answer matches the question's correct answer. The correctness comparison uses the shared comparator (`is_answer_correct` per V4.3 §10) that 04B's scoring path also uses — a pure function on a question record from Doc 02 and an answer string. This comparator handles question-type-aware comparison (letter equality for multiple-choice; numeric-equivalence for student-produced response). **Missing answer rows count as wrong** (per invariant \#13); the count uses INNER JOIN on actual submissions, equivalent to V4.3 §11's LEFT-JOIN-with-missing-as-wrong because both produce the same Module 1 correct count.  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:936:3. The routing decision is computed: `module2_path = (module1_raw >= threshold) ? 'B' : 'A'`.  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:937:4. In one transaction: section state goes to `module1_submitted`, `module2_path` is written, `module1_submitted_at = clock_timestamp()`, `module1_submitted_by` is set to `'student'` or `'timeout'` per the trigger.  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:940:**Important boundary clarification (V2.2 — reviewer mandate 5):** the routing-decision Module 1 raw-score computation is the only correctness math 04A performs. It is required because routing is an immediate runtime decision and cannot wait on 04B. Computing it uses the shared `is_answer_correct` comparator (a single pure function) and a COUNT(...) aggregate. **This does NOT constitute scoring.** 04A produces `module2_path` (an integer routing decision) — it does NOT produce scaled scores, ceilings, deductions, or floors. All scaled-score math lives in 04B V4.3.
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:944:Once written, `module2_path` is immutable. The schema enforces this via a trigger:
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:946:CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION enforce\_module2\_path\_immutability() RETURNS trigger AS $$  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:948:  IF OLD.module2\_path IS NOT NULL  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:949:     AND NEW.module2\_path IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.module2\_path THEN  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:950:    RAISE EXCEPTION 'module2\_path is immutable once set';  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:956:CREATE TRIGGER trg\_module2\_path\_immutability  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:958:  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION enforce\_module2\_path\_immutability();

docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:964:The routed path is NEVER surfaced to the student in any API response, UI element, or report field. It is captured in `test_session_sections.module2_path` for scoring (04B reads it to apply the correct M2 difficulty distribution) and audit. This decision exists to avoid encouraging students to over-interpret their routing as a performance signal — the routing exists to make scaled scores meaningful, not to be a metric in itself.

The state-read endpoint (§15.1) surfaces `module2_path_locked: boolean` to indicate whether routing has occurred, but never the path value itself.

The transition out of `section_break` is exclusively driven by the Math Module 1 start request. If the student lingers in `section_break` past `grace_expires_at`, the abandonment sweep finalizes the session per §14.

docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:1128:**Module 1 re-submit edge case.** Once Module 1 is in `module1_submitted` state, no further answer writes or module-submit requests against Module 1 succeed — the §4 \#6 invariant rejects them. The locked routing decision and locked answer set together define the section's Module 1 contribution to scoring, and neither can be modified after the first successful submit (whether student-initiated or timeout). This bounds the routing-immutability guarantee against any client-side bug or replay.

docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:1262:`section_state` per section identifies the actual terminal section state. `scoreable: true` is set only when `section_state = 'submitted'` (per invariant \#16: partial scoring eligibility requires Module 2 submitted). Sections that ended in any other state — including `module1_submitted` (Module 1 routed but Module 2 never reached submitted) — are flagged `scoreable: false`.
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:1266:**Why `module1_submitted` is not scoreable (BL4 clarification).** Routing locks a Module 2 path at Module 1 submission, but the locked path does NOT mean Module 2 was attempted. Scoring a section based only on Module 1 answers would require a separate "Module 1 only" scoring path in 04B, which V4.3 does not provide and Parent V3.0 does not commission. The clean rule is: a section produces a partial score only after Module 2 reaches `submitted` (whether by student submit or by Module 2 timeout, both of which write at least zero answers to Module 2 and produce a complete two-module input to V4.3's scoring formula).
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:1268:**Sweep classification edge case (V2.2 lock-cycle BL4 clarification).** Per §14.3 step 4, the sweep classifies a session as `partial_scored_abandoned` if at least one section ends in `submitted` state. A session abandoned with BOTH sections in `module1_submitted` (Module 1 timeout fired on both, Module 2 never started on either) ends as `abandoned_final` — no scoreable section means no outbox event and no `score_runs` row.

docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:1332:A subtle case: a student is in `module1_active` for RW, closes their browser, and returns 90 minutes later (longer than the 32-minute Module 1 duration). What happens?
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:1334:* **Lenient mode:** the section's `last_active_at` is roughly 90 minutes old. The pause-detection logic adds \~90 minutes to `active_paused_ms`. The remaining time is recomputed via §8.2 and is approximately what it was before browser-close (minus the few seconds before the last heartbeat). The student resumes with most of their Module 1 time intact.  
docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:1335:* **Strict mode:** `active_paused_ms` remains 0\. `remaining_ms` via §8.2 is `max(0, module1_expires_at - clock_timestamp())` which is 0\. The next request invokes the §8.4 timeout path: Module 1 auto-submits with `submitted_by = 'timeout'`, routing computes against whatever answers were stored before browser-close, and the section transitions to `module1_submitted`. The student can then start Module 2 normally.

docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:497:The canonical ID is an opaque durable identifier, not a taxonomic label. It carries only section and source-type information as structural prefixes. All other item metadata lives in the record per §16.

docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:594:The generator produces output matching §15. The upsert path (§27) maps generator output into this schema, assigns the canonical ID, and inserts or updates.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1050:Approved content publishes through idempotent upsert keyed by canonical ID.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1073:* Upsert by canonical ID prevents duplicate insertion  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1098:Idempotency lets the team re-run promotion without fear of duplicate insertion, which is essential for pipelines that include manual steps and occasional partial failures. Upsert by canonical ID is what makes idempotency possible — insert-only semantics would require distinguishing "already inserted" from "new" at every batch, which is fragile. The version increment on update preserves edit history without requiring explicit version management in the upsert caller, which removes a class of bugs where revisions overwrite history silently.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1116:`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE` keyed by canonical ID, likely called item-by-item rather than as a single batch transaction. Error handling likely aggregates per-item failures rather than rolling back the batch.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1163:* `staging_id`: uuid primary key (temporary, pre-canonical ID)  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1184:* On success, generates canonical IDs per §14 for each item, inserts into `public.questions`, records a row in `public.promotion_log`  
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1289:Revision (explanation fix, metadata correction, option text typo) uses the version log per §16 lineage: same canonical ID, version increment, diff stored in `question_versions`. Revised items go through QA again before republish.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1353:| Upsert | Canonical ID collision | Regenerate random segment, retry once; alert on second collision |
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1554:**Previous Rule:** Publishing logic implied inserts or generic writes. **Updated Rule:** Approved content uses idempotent upsert keyed by canonical ID per §27. **Why It Changed:** Safe re-runs, metadata upgrades, explanation upgrades, dedup prevention, operational resilience. **Build Impact:** All publishing jobs must be idempotent. `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE` is the canonical pattern.
docs/Spec/Lyceon — Document 02A_ Question Generation & Content Supply Chain (V6).md:1566:**Previous Rule:** Canonical ID generation authority undefined. **Updated Rule:** Canonical IDs are generated product-side at promotion time per §14. `Lyceonquestions` never issues IDs that reach `public.questions`. **Why It Changed:** ID authority belongs with the system that owns the live bank. Prevents generation-repo compromise or bug from producing duplicate or malformed IDs. Enables collision checking against live data without granting broad live-table access to the generation repo. **Build Impact:** Generation pipeline produces candidates without `id`. Staging uses temporary `staging_id` (uuid). Promotion job assigns canonical ID at insertion.

docs/SpecAudit/10-gap-registry/gap-registry.md:142:| GAP-HY-13 | HIGH              | DRIFT         | **Code-vs-genesis drift on `account_deletion_requests`** (caused a live prod outage: `/api/profile` 503 on all logins). The deletion-service code (`server/middleware/supabase-auth.ts`, `server/routes/account-deletion-routes.ts`) was written against the **pre-baseline legacy** table shape (`user_id`, `executed_at`); the governed genesis (`00000000000000_genesis.sql:245`) + drift snapshot + live prod all use `profile_id` + `completion_at`. The middleware deletion-status read failed on the absent columns → fail-closed `503 DELETION_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE` on every authenticated request. **Column-name drift FIXED** (PR #402, forward code patch, no DB change — prod ≡ genesis is canonical, the code was the drifted side; renamed every reference across both files). **Structural + window drift FIXED** (follow-up PR): the `/delete` insert now supplies the canonical NOT-NULL columns `scheduled_hard_delete_at` (= requested*at + **7 days**, Doc-01 §40.2) and `actor_profile_id` (= the requesting user, §5/§40.2), plus `stripe_cancellation_status='pending'` (§40.2.1); the `execute-deletions` cron now selects `WHERE scheduled_hard_delete_at <= now()` (§40.5) instead of the prior `requested_at < now-24h` (the 24h grace contradicted the locked 7-day window). Prod had **0 deletion rows** — the path never worked (a live right-to-erasure gap), now restored. **Residual OPEN (deferred, cohesive increment):** the §40.3 soft-delete login-lock (`profiles.deleted_at` set on request + auth middleware rejecting login during grace) and §40.4 email-link recovery must ship **together** — `requireSupabaseAuth` bakes in the deletion block (so a `deleted_at` login-lock would strand the authenticated `/cancel-deletion`), and setting `deleted_at` alone frees the email via `idx_profiles_email_active WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` (a re-signup during a recoverable grace would break cancel). The de-identify named writer `deletion-service.ts` does not exist; the live writer is `account-deletion-routes.ts`. **Mediated-delete actor (captured for the §40.3/40.4 increment so it is not missed):** §5 (L201) — `actor_profile_id` *"may be the profile itself for self-service, or an admin."_ #403's self-serve `/delete` correctly sets actor = the requesting student. Deletion is **student- or admin-initiated only** (L2011: _"Guardian cannot prevent the deletion (student or admin-initiated)"\_) — **guardians CANNOT initiate deletion** (view-only), so there is no guardian-initiated delete path. The future admin-initiated (support-mediated) delete must set `actor_profile_id = admin_id` + `on_behalf_of_profile_id = student_id` (+ `ticket_id`/`justification`, L2118 support pattern), **not** the student as actor. **§40.3 lock + §40.4 recovery NOW BUILT** (this branch): atomic `request_account_deletion` + `restore_account_deletion` (token recovery) RPCs staged in `migrations-pending/`; server code (V2 `/delete`, token-gated `/recover-deletion`, middleware `deleted_at` login-lock) is **flag-gated OFF** (`ACCOUNT_DELETION_LIFECYCLE_V2`) so it ships dormant and activates atomically on owner-apply — strand-safe (recovery carries no session; proven by the load-bearing cancel-mid-grace test). **Codex chain-of-custody audit (2026-06-21) found the destructive executor was NOT actually gated** — `/api/account/execute-deletions` ran the §40.5 selector + `deidentify_user` regardless of the flag and was reachable by any admin, falsifying "flag-OFF dormant" for the one endpoint that does irreversible work. **FIXED (this branch):** the executor body is now the pure `executeDueDeletions()` whose ONLY caller is `POST /api/internal/execute-deletions` — **CRON_SECRET-gated** (mounted on the internal cron router beside the legal-acceptance drain; unauthorized/unconfigured → 404, fails closed) AND **flag-gated** (`ACCOUNT_DELETION_LIFECYCLE_V2` OFF → inert no-op acknowledgement, no selector, no `deidentify_user`). The old admin route is removed, so flag-OFF is genuinely dormant and nothing but the scheduled job (with the flag on) can reach the irreversible path. **CLOSED-PENDING-ACTIVATION (2026-06-22, #410/#411 → cleanup → main):** the full vertical is built + merged (#403 insert/cron, #406 executor gating + global soft-lock + bypass fix, #407 atomic cancel, #408 UI + flag-on e2e, #410 curated error mapper) and the staged migration was OWNER-APPLIED to prod then RECONCILED into the governed set (#411: `git mv` into supabase/migrations/, snapshot regenerated +175/−0, genesis-fresh-apply + all four deletion gates green) so prod ≡ governed ≡ snapshot. Remaining is owner-gated ACTIVATION only — flip ACCOUNT_DELETION_LIFECYCLE_V2 — plus the §40.3/§40.6 spec edits (HY-16/HY-14, owner-applied to the read-only corpus) and the ledger migration-repair (owner-run, or self-healing on the next governed db push). | FIX-CODE (#403 names/insert/cron; §40.3/40.4 built — flag-gated + staged; executor now flag + cron-secret gated) | BUILT + PROD-RECONCILED — dormant; ACTIVATION owner-gated (#411 → main 2026-06-22; prod ≡ governed ≡ snapshot; flag OFF)                                                                                                                                        |
docs/SpecAudit/10-gap-registry/gap-registry.md:143:| GAP-HY-14 | HIGH              | RESOLVED      | **Under-13 deletion window — locked-spec contradiction RESOLVED by counsel (uniform 7-day).** §40.6 fires only for under-13 accounts on **guardian consent revocation (§37.5) or expiry (§37.4)** — a guardian-consent trigger, NOT the self-serve `/delete` route (correctly out of GAP-HY-13). The locked spec self-contradicted on the window: §37.5 _"after 7 days"_ vs §40.6 _"immediate… without the 7-day grace period."_ **Counsel resolution (2026-06-20): under-13 follows the standard 7-day deletion path — there is NO accelerated/"immediate" branch.** Consequence: the under-13 path is the **existing §40.2–§40.5 soft-delete → hard-delete flow applied to under-13 — no new deletion code**; only the _trigger_ differs (guardian consent revocation/expiry vs self-serve), and that trigger is itself gated on the §37.5 consent-revocation feature landing (separate work). §37.4 expiry keeps its separate `consent_expiration_deletion_days` (default **30 days** from signup) — a distinct pre-deletion timer, unaffected. **Spec de-contradiction:** the §40.6 edit (retitle "Under-13 deletion (consent revoked or expired)"; body → "standard §40.2–§40.5 flow on the uniform 7-day grace window… consistent with §37.5") is **PREPARED but pending owner-apply** — `docs/Spec/` is a hard READ-ONLY guardrail (tool-denied), so the canonical edit must be applied at the spec source by Karl. docs/SpecAudit/10-gap-registry/gap-registry.md:144:| GAP-HY-15 | HIGH (compliance) | MISSING       | **The `deidentify_user` RPC the hard-delete cron calls does not exist — right-to-erasure never _completes_.** `server/routes/account-deletion-routes.ts:202` (the `execute-deletions` cron) calls `admin.rpc('deidentify_user', { target_user_id, deleted_email })`, but **no such function is defined in `supabase/` (genesis or any migration)** — verified by grep. Post-#403 a user can _request_ deletion (insert + 7-day schedule now work), but at T+7 the cron's RPC call errors → `failureCount++`, the request stays `status='pending'`, and the PII is **retained indefinitely past the promised 7-day window** (GDPR Art. 17 / COPPA erasure obligation unmet). No active leak and back-fillable (once the RPC lands the cron picks up the stuck `pending` rows), but the deletion lifecycle is **not end-to-end functional**. Fix = author the §40.5 `deidentify_user(target_user_id uuid, deleted_email text)` SECURITY-DEFINER RPC (exact body specced in §40.5: the `profiles` anonymization UPDATE + feature-table hard-deletes per Doc 03A retention + anonymization-retention window), mirroring the existing `guardian_can_view_student` RPC style. **Migration is OWNER-APPLIED** — stage in `supabase/migrations-pending/`, Karl activates (`migrations-pending/README.md`). Destructive + retention-sensitive → the feature-table delete list must trace to Doc 03A V2 retention before applying. **Core RPC NOW STAGED** (this branch): `deidentify_user(target_user_id uuid, deleted_email text)` — CORE profiles anonymization only (per owner ruling "core anonymization first") — staged in `migrations-pending/20260621000000_account_deletion_lifecycle.sql` with the feature-table cascade left as a Doc 03A-retention-gated TODO. The cron caller already matches the signature; erasure completes end-to-end once the migration is applied. **Destructive-path rehearsal NOW PROVEN (this branch):** `scripts/ci/deletion-deidentify-rehearsal.{sh,sql}` + a hard CI gate (`deletion-deidentify-rehearsal`) apply genesis + the staged migration to a throwaway Postgres and prove, against the REAL schema (real `idx_profiles_email_active`, real `profiles_set_age` trigger), that `deidentify_user` is **exact-target** (seeds one eligible + active/mid-grace/already-anonymized personas; anonymizes ONLY the eligible row, every other row byte-identical via `md5(to_jsonb(row))`) and **idempotent/re-entrant** (re-run over an already-anonymized row is a PII-safe no-op; once `status='completed'` the cron selection excludes it so a double-run cannot re-touch/strand) — with a negative control proving the gate RAISEs if the WHERE clause is broken. This is genesis-fresh-apply discipline for the irreversible path: rehearsal-on-non-prod before Karl owner-applies. **Negative control NOW a committed CI gate** (Codex 2026-06-21 flagged the first one as an uncommitted local one-off — for a destructive-path gate that = no negative control): `scripts/ci/deletion-deidentify-negative-control.sh` mutates `deidentify_user` to drop its `WHERE` on a throwaway copy, runs the SAME rehearsal SQL, and asserts it FAILS specifically at exact-target assertion (B); the shared throwaway-DB setup is factored into `scripts/ci/lib/deletion-rehearsal-db.sh` (no duplication), and the control runs as a second step of the `deletion-deidentify-rehearsal` CI job — so the rehearsal's ability-to-fail is CI-enforced + repeatable. **CLOSURE (2026-06-22, #410/#411 → main):** the core `deidentify_user` RPC was OWNER-APPLIED to prod and reconciled into the governed migration set (prod ≡ governed ≡ snapshot); the three rehearsal/e2e scripts were hardened to run on a real Supabase DB — each is now a single self-cleaning DO block (editor-portable, prod-safe, re-runnable, zero residue) — and stay green incl. the committed negative control. CORE profiles-PII anonymization is now end-to-end; the feature-table cascade (tutor store + Doc-05-derived tables + ledgers, tracked as TU-03) remains OPEN, gated on Doc 03A V2 retention sign-off.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | STAGE-MIGRATION (owner-applies; rehearsal + negative-control gates prove it pre-apply)                           | PARTIAL — core RPC APPLIED to prod + governed (#411 → main 2026-06-22); rehearsal/e2e gates now editor-portable + self-cleaning + green; feature-table cascade still OPEN (Doc 03A retention / TU-03)                                                           |
docs/SpecAudit/10-gap-registry/gap-registry.md:145:| GAP-HY-16 | HIGH (security)   | MISSING+DRIFT | **§40.3 login-lock — model change (hard→soft, per owner) + an audit-missed bypass class, both fixed structurally.** Karl (2026-06-21) chose the **soft-lock** model over the as-built hard-lock: a grace-window (soft-deleted, request still pending) user CAN log in but only into a restricted pending-deletion state (in-app cancel), instead of a blunt 403 + email-link-only recovery. **Audit-missed finding (Codex chain-of-custody cleared the requireSupabaseAuth path only):** the §40.3 lock was enforced _per-route_ inside `requireSupabaseAuth`, but the runtime surfaces use `requireRequestUser` (no deletion check) — `tutor-runtime`, `full-length-exam-routes`, `review-session-routes`, `questions-runtime`, `profile-routes`, `guardian-role` (30+ call sites). Since a grace-window user can obtain a _fresh_ Supabase session (auth user isn't banned until hard-delete), they could still reach tutor/exam/review/questions during the 7-day grace — the lock didn't actually hold (dormant only because flag-off). **FIXED structurally (this branch, flag-gated/dormant):** (1) resolver now distinguishes `pending_deletion` (deleted_at set, request pending → recoverable) from `deleted` (completed → gone); (2) a single global **`enforceDeletionLock`** middleware (mounted after `supabaseAuthMiddleware`, before all API routers) **default-denies every /api route** for deleted/pending users with a minimal pending-only allowlist — `GET /api/profile`, `POST /api/account/cancel-deletion`, `/recover-deletion`, `POST /api/auth/signout` — and the per-route `requireSupabaseAuth` deletion check is REMOVED (one enforcement point, can't diverge; new routes locked by default); (3) hard-deleted → 403 `ACCOUNT_DELETED` everywhere (no allowlist); (4) in-app cancel (`/cancel-deletion` V2) clears `deleted_at` to lift the lock (safety order: cancel request first, then clear; email-reclaim 23505 → 409); (5) `/api/profile` carries server-authority `featureFlags.accountDeletionLifecycleV2` + `pendingDeletion.scheduledHardDeleteAt` so the client routes to the pending screen (never a client env guess). Non-/api paths never blocked (SPA must load). Flag-OFF ⇒ pure pass-through. Tests: allowlist + strand-prevention (pending reaches every allowlisted route, 403 elsewhere), hard-deleted 403, flag-off pass-through. **Spec edit owed (owner-applied):** §40.3 must change from "user cannot log in (403)" to the soft-lock + allowlist model — `docs/Spec/` is READ-ONLY (tool-denied), text handed to Karl in the PR. **Still TODO this vertical:** UI (delete trigger, recovery page, pending screen) + a flag-on e2e + re-audit. **DONE (2026-06-22, #408/#410 → main):** the UI shipped (DeleteAccountCard, PendingDeletionScreen, /account/recover), the flag-on e2e shipped and was hardened to a prod-safe self-cleaning DO block, and delete/cancel error display was routed through a curated never-raw-string mapper (account-deletion-errors.ts) — Codex chain-of-custody PASS. Remaining is the §40.3 spec edit (owner-applied to the read-only corpus) + flag activation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | FIX-CODE (structural global lock; spec edit owner-applied)                                                       | PARTIAL — backend soft-lock + bypass fix + UI + flag-on e2e + curated error mapper SHIPPED (#408/#410 → main 2026-06-22); remaining = §40.3 spec edit (owner) + flag activation                                                                                 |
docs/SpecAudit/10-gap-registry/gap-registry.md:146:| GAP-HY-20 | MEDIUM            | MISSING       | **Canonical-ID invariant CI enforcement (INV-05D-18).** `student_id` is THE canonical column name for the per-profile UUID on every feature table; `user_id` as a profile-reference column name is FORBIDDEN for new tables going forward. docs/SpecAudit/pre_impl_verification_05d.md:272:In **anonymized-retention mode** (Q5 default once privacy sign-off clears), Layer 2 anonymizes the derived aggregates (`mastery_event_audit_log`, `mastery_domain_refresh_audit_log`, mastery/KPI/projection tables) with a one-way `gen_random_uuid()` surrogate. But Layer 1 **hard-deletes** these two event source tables — the raw event stream is destroyed while the derived aggregates survive anonymized.
docs/SpecAudit/pre_impl_verification_05d.md:274:**Asymmetry:** the ML-retention value of anonymized-retention lives in the event stream (per-question, per-difficulty, per-timestamp granularity), not in the pre-aggregated mastery scores. If the source events are hard-deleted while the aggregates are retained, the anonymized data has no re-derivation path and limited ML utility.
docs/SpecAudit/pre_impl_verification_05d.md:276:**Q9: In anonymized-retention mode, do the raw event source tables (`practice_session_items`, `review_error_attempts`) get hard-deleted (Layer 1) or anonymized (Layer 2 surrogate)?**
docs/SpecAudit/pre_impl_verification_05d.md:278:**Q9=(a) ANSWERED:** Event-source tables are **anonymized-and-retained** (Layer 2). Owner ruling: every response is world-model training corpus — event-stream preservation is a platform invariant. The ML-retention value lives in the per-event stream (per-question, per-difficulty, per-timestamp granularity), not the pre-aggregated mastery scores.
docs/SpecAudit/pre_impl_verification_05d.md:286:This means steps 1–3 and 5–6 are ALL Layer 2 in anonymized-retention mode (not just the event-source steps 1 and 5). Only step 4 (`review_schedule`, no FK from retained tables) remains Layer 1 hard-delete.
docs/SpecAudit/pre_impl_verification_05d.md:302:**Strategy B — Parent-first CASCADE-reliant:** Delete `review_sessions` (CASCADE auto-deletes `review_session_items` → `review_error_attempts`), then delete `review_schedule`. **Pro:** fewer statements. **Con:** CASCADE-deleted row counts are invisible to the function's delete verification; mixing explicit + implicit deletion makes targeting harder to prove in test.
docs/SpecAudit/pre_impl_verification_05d.md:304:**Committed strategy: A (children-first explicit).** Rationale: for a PERMANENT irreversible hard-delete, every deleted row must be counted and verified. CASCADE hides row counts and makes the exact-target test (§10 rehearsal requirement) unable to assert per-table deletion counts. The same children-first approach applies to practice tables (`practice_session_items` → `practice_sessions`).

docs/Spec/Doc 04A — Exam Runtime & Session State.md:1068:   * **Body-mismatch audit (V2.2 lock-cycle HIGH1).** Before returning the stored response, compare the inbound request's `(section, module, question_id, ordinal, answer)` to the stored row's same fields. If any differ, the client is reusing an idempotency key with a different payload — a likely client bug. The server STILL returns the original `response_json` (idempotency contract preserved; canonical state untouched) but additionally emits an `idempotency_body_mismatch` audit event recording the inbound fields vs the stored fields. This is observability, not rejection — the canonical contract for replay is "same key → same response," regardless of inbound body. Do NOT introduce `idempotency_conflict` as a hard rejection unless a future contract revision requires it.
